scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a config change on r2, r10 (which is in area 4) lost its
OSPF adjacency to r2 and its routing table collapsed -- every
route beyond area 4 vanished from r10's RIB and hosts behind
r10 lost the backbone. r2 reports area 4 stub configuration is
no longer active. What's wrong?

post_inject_check.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r2 OSPF area 4 stub designation
Mechanism: Area 4 was originally configured as a stub on BOTH
  r2 (ABR) and r10 (internal). The stub flag (Hello E-bit)
  must MATCH between neighbors: when r2 drops `area 4 stub`,
  r10 (still stub) rejects r2's Hellos, and after the dead
  interval (~40 s) the r2<->r10 adjacency DROPS. r2 is r10's
  ONLY OSPF neighbor, so r10 is isolated from the OSPF domain:
  its OSPF RIB collapses to intra-area entries (lab-verified
  2026-07-12: 61 -> 13 `show ip route ospf` lines, neighbor
  table empty, zero external LSAs -- NOT an external-flood
  RIB bloat).
Localization: r2 (the ABR is responsible for area type config)
Root cause: `area 4 stub` missing from r2's OSPF process
Fix: `vtysh -c "router ospf" -c "area 4 stub"` on r2
scoring_axes: must-explain-adjacency-loss: stub-flag (Hello E-bit) mismatch causes the r2<->r10 adjacency to drop, isolating area 4

line.command: vtysh -c "show ip ospf neighbor" | grep -c Full

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is an OSPF stub-area type mismatch on the segment I link between r2 (eth2,
21.x.x.x) and r10 (eth0). r10 has area 0.0.0.4 declared as a stub area
(`area 4 stub` is present in its running config), which causes it to set the
E-bit to 0 in every OSPF Hello it sends. r2, after its recent configuration
change, no longer has an `area 0.0.0.4 stub` statement — area 4 is now treated
as a normal (non-stub) area on r2's side, so r2's Hellos carry E-bit = 1. Per
RFC 2328 §10.5, when two routers disagree on the E-bit in the Hello Options
field they must discard each other's Hellos; adjacency formation cannot proceed
past the Init state. As a result, r2 and r10 have zero OSPF neighbors in area 4,
r2 (the ABR) never injects a default route into the stub, and r10's RIB contains
only its own directly connected prefixes — all inter-area and external routes are
absent, cutting off every host behind r10 (segment DD, 100.x/8, 110.x/8) from
the rest of the network.

Root cause: the `area 0.0.0.4 stub` line was removed from r2's OSPF configuration
during the config change, creating a stub-type mismatch with r10.

Fix: on r2, enter OSPF configuration and add `area 4 stub`, then save (`write
memory`). This realigns the E-bit on both peers, Hellos will be accepted,
adjacency will reform, and r2 will resume injecting the default summary route
into the stub area restoring full reachability for r10 and its downstream hosts.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identifies r2 as the device missing the 'area 4 stub' statement and prescribes adding it on r2 to restore adjacency.
The writeup explicitly identifies the OSPF area 4 stub configuration/E-bit mismatch (missing `area 4 stub` on r2) as the faulty component.

per_axis.axis: must-explain-adjacency-loss: stub-flag (Hello E-bit) mismatch causes the r2<->r10 adjacency to drop, isolating area 4
per_axis.rationale: The agent correctly explains that the Hello E-bit (stub flag) mismatch caused Hellos to be discarded, breaking the r2–r10 adjacency and isolating area 4.
Adds the missing 'area 4 stub' on r2 (and saves), which matches the expected fix and will restore adjacency and default injection.

The agent gathered both routers' OSPF configs and live neighbor state, observed the stub-flag mismatch and missing adjacencies, and produced a diagnosis that follows OSPF behavior for E-bit mismatches. Most key observations are present in the log (configs requested, r10 has no neighbors, r2 shows a neighbor only in area 0), and the causal chain from mismatched stub flag → Hello rejection → adjacency loss → r10 RIB collapse is correct and complete.
